primary_claim: Training 20 rank-2 LoRA adapters on Qwen1.5-14B-instruct with a modified KL-divergence objective to unsupervisedly explore new behaviours, 25% (5 of 20) of the resulting behaviours reduce to clean, linear, steerable concept vectors (via mean activation difference) that reliably reproduce the LoRA's behavioural shift when applied as a steering vector.

effect.metric: linearity score (cosine-similarity-based match between LoRA behaviour and extracted vector behaviour)
effect.value: 5 of 20 trained LoRAs (25%) yield clean linear, interpretable, steerable vectors; linearity scores ranged ~0.71-0.86 across the 20 vectors

stated_future_work: Validate the hypothesis that the extracted vector is a linear combination of a 'character' vector and an 'alliteration' vector
Run ablations on dataset design to reduce the number of non-generalizable behaviours
Explore why a brash/rude LoRA behaviour could not be captured by its corresponding linear vector
limitations_stated: Did not have time to run ablations on why one vector's behaviour didn't generalize from its LoRA
Train and test datasets shared scenarios (with different prompts), which the author notes 'may not be ideal'
quote: I trained 20 LoRAs on Qwen1.5-14b-instruct, out of which five correspond to linear, steerable, and interpretable vectors.
